author: ojiudezue
title: Harness adopts always-on agent patterns: durable due dates, a decisions queue, one writer per tree, quiet on non-events
summary: Against claude.com's 'building always-on agents' guide, the orchestration harness had five gaps seen in one day: a mutating reviewer sharing a worktree with readers (void passes twice), duplicate reports and ~20 no-news pings answered with status lines, follow-ups held only in-session (the 10:00 v5.108.37 release was missed), a memory index carrying stale pickups, and operator decisions piling up as chat lists. Operator approved all five fixes: one writer per tree and report-once/quiet rules (memory), due: fields on cards surfaced at session start and by --check exit 4, a Decisions view on the hosted board with one-tap PICK buttons, and a memory archive.
why: Each gap produced a concrete failure the same day: reviews redone, operator chat noise, a release shipped 8 hours late because the timer lived in my head, and Q-F1..Q-F4 re-listed across several messages. The guide's patterns map one-to-one and are cheap.
alternatives_considered: Scheduled cloud triggers for follow-ups (rejected: no local repo/HA access, a second place to look)
A new approvals endpoint (rejected: the board's disposition queue already exists)
implications: Follow-ups now outlive a session; any promised time goes on a card as due:. Agents must report once. The same guide reframes OC (detect, triage, route rather than diagnose), pending the operator's call.
revisit_trigger: A due item missed despite the hook, or decisions still answered in chat instead of the queue
